connexins 32 and 43 are expressed in the brain, and that their expression is developmentally regulated.
gap junction proteins are differentially expressed in brain cells, and this expression pattern changes during brain development.
connexin 33, a gap junction protein expressed primarily in the brain, is a product of a gene that is expressed in a tissue-specific manner and that is regulated during brain development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of gap junction proteins and their functional roles during brain maturation.
the expression of gap junction proteins in the central nervous system.
the molecular basis of gap junction formation and the role of gap junctions in the development and function of the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of connexins is not only cell type-specific but also developmentally regulated in brain tissues.

gap junctions are not a homogeneous group of channels but rather a heterogeneous group with different connexin subtypes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gap junctions in the brain are different from other tissues in their expression and function.
gap junctions are present in the brain and that their presence is regulated in a cell- and stage-specific fashion.
gap junction proteins are expressed in specific cell types in adult brain and are differentially expressed during brain development.

the expression of different gap junction proteins in the brain may be important in the development and function of this organ.
